summary_en: This study compares elritercept with epoetin alfa to treat anemia in adults with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome who need regular red blood cell transfusions. Elritercept is given as a subcutaneous injection starting at 3.75 mg/kg once every 4 weeks, with a possible increase to 5.0 mg/kg, while epoetin alfa is given as a subcutaneous injection starting at 450 IU/kg once weekly, with a possible increase up to 1050 IU/kg (maximum 80,000 IU). The main aim is to measure how much elritercept reduces the need for red blood cell transfusions and raises hemoglobin levels, and this is a Phase 3 study.
summary_es: Este estudio compara elritercept con epoetina alfa para tratar la anemia en adultos con síndrome mielodisplásico de bajo riesgo que necesitan transfusiones regulares de glóbulos rojos. El elritercept se administra como inyección subcutánea a partir de 3,75 mg/kg una vez cada 4 semanas, con posible aumento a 5,0 mg/kg, mientras que la epoetina alfa se administra como inyección subcutánea a partir de 450 UI/kg una vez por semana, con posible aumento hasta 1050 UI/kg (máximo 80 000 UI). El objetivo principal es medir cuánto reduce el elritercept la necesidad de transfusiones de glóbulos rojos y cuánto eleva los niveles de hemoglobina, y este es un estudio de Fase 3.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (very low, low, or intermediate IPSS-R risk).
Needs 2 to 6 red blood cell transfusions over at least 8 weeks before randomization.
Has not had prior epoetin alfa or darbepoetin, or only within the limits the protocol allows.
not_for: Myelodysplastic syndrome with del(5q), unclassifiable, or secondary myelodysplastic syndrome.
Known history of acute myeloid leukemia.
Anemia from other known causes, such as thalassemia or hemolytic anemia.
Significant heart disease, recent clotting event, or ejection fraction below 35%.
Other cancer within the past 3 years, apart from the exceptions listed in the criteria.
